N-1.8-A.skill: reason about how correcting an outlying value changes (and does not change) a modified boxplot, fences, whiskers and summary statistics

N-1.8-B.skill: interpret what a boxplot does and does not show about proportions of data, skew and shape

N-1.9-A.skill: choose resistant or non-resistant summaries to compare two distributions given skew and outliers

N-1.9-B.skill: compare two distributions from five-number summaries without confusing box size, extremes and sample size

N-1.10-A.skill: distinguish parameters from statistics and explain why statistics vary from sample to sample

N-1.10-B.skill: judge whether a data-collection plan matches the population, groups and variable named in the question

N-1.11-A.skill: recognize why equal individual chances do not make a sample a simple random sample

N-1.11-B.skill: carry out simple random selection with a table of random digits, handling invalid labels and repeats

N-1.12-A.skill: identify the type of sampling bias in a scenario and the likely direction of the error

N-1.12-B.skill: choose a change that reduces bias and know that larger samples do not remove bias

N-1.13-A.skill: find the confounding flaw in an experiment design and choose the best fix

N-1.13-B.skill: determine the scope of conclusions (cause, generalization) from random assignment and random selection
